title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Tech rebounded Monday — Nasdaq Composite +1.1%, S&P 500 +0.4%, Dow -0.1% (-36 pts); futures point higher into today's open (S&P 500 futures +0.44%, Nasdaq 100 futures +1.19%, Dow futures flat).

Markets: 10-year Treasury yield near 5.14%, among the highest in decades; WTI crude ~$98-99/bbl (up ~15% over two weeks on Houthi tanker-attack fears); gold ~$4,140/oz pressured by the dollar/yields; bitcoin ~$82k. Fed futures price only ~17% odds of a hike at the Oct 27-28 FOMC.

Companies: Heavy earnings day — GE Aerospace, GM, Halliburton, Northrop Grumman and RTX report before the open; Netflix and SpaceX report after the close (Netflix options imply a ~9% swing). Premarket: RTX -1.9%, Northrop -2%.

Companies: Cleveland-Cliffs jumped 16% after guiding to its best 2027 profit since 2021; Elon Musk pledged a SpaceX share to every U.S. child (~$10B total); Two Sigma co-founder John Overdeck faces a divorce trial that could shift control of the $85B quant fund.

Macro/Policy: Saudi Arabia postponed its 'Davos in the Desert' investor conference over Houthi-attack security concerns; AI-infrastructure jitters persist after last week's CoreWeave-led selloff; Anthropic unveiled a public-benefit fund pledging 5% of its shares (up to $100B at a $2T IPO valuation).
